full_judgment:
5. The heirs of the original plaintiff (respondent Nos.1-4) preferred appeal, Title Appeal No. 35 of 1992, and the learned Subordinate Judge, Shariatpur by his judgment and decree dated 3-11-93 allowed the appeal, set aside the decree of the trial Court and decreed the suit holding, inter alia, that defendant No.1 (appellant) could not discharge his onus to prove that the documents relating to the auction purchase are forged and collusive. The appellant then moved the High Court Division in revision against the judgment and decree of the lower appellate Court, Civil Revision No. 1191 of 1994, which was summarily rejected by a Single Bench of the High Court Division on 16-1-94. Leave was granted to consider whether the High Court Division erred in law in rejecting the revisional application summarily when the judgment of the lower appellate Court, a judgment of reversal, does not patently show that it reversed in the trial Court's finding on possession of the appellant in the disputed land and also does not show that it adverted to the trial Court's reasoning for disbelieving Ext. 1, 1(Ka), 3 and 3(Ka) as to the alleged certificate sale of the suit land. 

 6. Mr. Md. Fazlul Karim, learned Advocate for the appellant, submitted that the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division erred in rejecting the revisional application of the appellant summarily, without considering that the judgment of the lower appellate Court was not at all a proper judgment of reversal, The trial Court, he submits, upon assigning reasons disbelieved the evidence of the PWs as regard the alleged possession of the plaintiff in the disputed land and further found that Ext .1, Ext.1(ka), Ext. 3, Ext. 3(ka) are forged, fabricated and ante-dated documents, but the lower appellate Court without reversing those findings of fact and traversing the reasoning’s assigned therefore illegally reversed the decree of the trial Court by simply observing that the appellant did not discharge his onus to prove that those documents are forged, etc. The lower appellate Court merely relied upon Auction Register No. 10, which was brought before the appellate Court on behalf of the heirs of the plaintiff at the time of hearing of the appeal. The appellant objected to the said Register on the ground that the entries made therein were made subsequent to the issuance of Ext. Ga, the information slip dated 15-1-87 issued to the appellant by the concerned Certificate Officer showing that no certificate case 92 CPT/62-63 had ever been initiated against the appellant in respect of the disputed property for arrears of rent. The trial Court disbelieved the plaintiff's information slip Ext. 3, as a fabricated one. The lower appellate Court dismissed the appellant's objection merely on surmise, without discarding Ext. Ga.
